predecessors.name: Essequibo
predecessors.text: Demerara and Essequibo, ceded by the Netherlands: 'The Netherlands officially ceded the three colonies to the United Kingdom' in the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814

predecessors.name: Berbice
predecessors.text: the colony of Berbice, the third of the 'three colonies' ceded in 1814

successors.name: Guyana
successors.text: 'Guyana became independent of the United Kingdom on 26 May 1966.'

ledger.x: 13 August 1814: the Netherlands cedes Demerara, Essequibo and Berbice to Britain.
21 July 1831: the three colonies are consolidated as British Guiana.
1895: the Venezuela boundary dispute becomes a crisis.
3 October 1899: the Paris tribunal awards Britain the Essequibo.
1899: the dispute is settled by arbitration (Treaty of Arbitration signed in Washington on 2 February 1897; Paris award 3 October 1899; border surveyed and 'signed off' in 1905).
26 May 1966: British Guiana becomes independent Guyana.

wars.name: Guyana–Venezuela territorial dispute
wars.outcome: Arbitration, not war: Schomburgk surveyed the line in 1840; Britain declared it the provisional frontier in October 1886; the Treaty of Arbitration was signed on 2 February 1897; the Paris award of 3 October 1899 gave Britain most of the land; the frontier…

certainty.note: The Schomburgk line was only a provisional frontier (1886) and the interior was not surveyed.
The Venezuelan frontier follows the 1899 award, surveyed in 1905; the New River Triangle on the Suriname side and the Brazilian frontier (not on the pages opened) are the exceptions.
